Thanks for this commit! For next time (and ideally here), please follow https://cbea.ms/git-commit/ for commit msgs and wrap the body at 72 chars, not a custom length. 

`Wrap the body at 72 characters`
sorry bout that. I think I have it right this time.

not really sure where this conclusion came from, but (at least to my understanding) it's not correct.  MinValue and MaxValue are required for IPMI to build SDRs, so they're arguably implemented by every sensor.

Thresholds I agree, are optional, and probably 50/50 for whether or not they're defined.

> MinValue and MaxValue are required for IPMI to build SDRs, so they're arguably implemented by every sensor.

This arguable but not true. ;)

1) I know for certain phosphor-virtual-sensor _only_ emits a {Min,Max}Value if one is explicitly enabled in the config, which is not required and many do not.

2) PLDM doesn't implement these in some cases.  https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/0b06dd891c42103a4555a0376e7a47b604f01ca9/platform-mc/numeric_sensor.cpp#L482

3) Not everyone uses IPMI so there is no certainty that anyone is testing even the IPMI side of it.

> > MinValue and MaxValue are required for IPMI to build SDRs, so they're arguably implemented by every sensor.
> 
> This arguable but not true. ;)
> 
> 1) I know for certain phosphor-virtual-sensor _only_ emits a {Min,Max}Value if one is explicitly enabled in the config, which is not required and many do not.

I said they were implemented, which we agree on.  Maybe it requires something defined in a config, but it does have an implementation.

> 
> 2) PLDM doesn't implement these in some cases.  https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/0b06dd891c42103a4555a0376e7a47b604f01ca9/platform-mc/numeric_sensor.cpp#L482

But it still implements them.

> 
> 3) Not everyone uses IPMI so there is no certainty that anyone is testing even the IPMI side of it.

Fair.  FWIW, I read the commit message first before I saw the code content.  Commit message seems pretty reasonable, and I'm not here to be a stickler for commit messages, so closing this out.

> so closing this out.

👍

```
2) PLDM doesn't implement these in some cases. https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/0b06dd891c42103a4555a0376e7a47b604f01ca9/platform-mc/numeric_sensor.cpp#L482

But it still implements them.
```

For some reason there are two different constructors in PLDM.  One of them doesn't implement (the one I linked to).  It just sets the value to NaN.
I think they're often set to NaN and not Inf?
Not in my experience. I did not see NaN.

This isn't really correct.  null in redfish means "supported but not yet populated".  Non existence for threshold on dbus has classically meant not supported.  we need to grok that distinction, and ideally in this commit message back it up with spec language.
Fixed the language to indicate that its not-populated.
Redfish service validator?

Done! Sorry, all our systems use mTLS and at least the host I had did not have password enabled, so I could not test it. Eventually, I realized I could do the testing on QEMU and a container with the npm package for RF validator.

Alternatively, go add support for mtls auth to redfish service validator and save yourself some time in the future.

Wit that said, qemu works so long as you can hit the code you’re changing.
Done
So Redfish validator was ran and happy? I don't see it mentioned in the Tested section.

> npm package for RF validator.

Redfish service validator is a python package......  Possibly you meant pip?

Overall, there's more issues with the commit message more than the actual diff, which really shouldn't hold things up.

Lets just be consistent, which should simplify the code, and then this should be good to go.
7 year old TODO here 😊

Don't statically allocate maps at runtime.  They consume memory in inconsistent ways.

If this is staying, just declare as an array of string_view, and use std::find_if.

Also, if we end up keeping, please sort lists like this.  The order here is semi-random.
Acknowledged
Is there any reason we limit this list?  This was limited to Value initially because that was where unavailable was, but in theory we could just make this not a per-value branch?
Yeah. No reason. I will remove this entire abomination and just set it to nullptr.
Acknowledged
I'd much rather we keep this flow simple, and have the same behavior for each one.  If they're present but non finite, we populate with null.
ok. I can do that. Agreed its a lot simpler and less ugly.
Acknowledged

Not sure what system you tested on, but this isn't the expected behavior of this patch, and is incorrect on Redfish.

You can't have a max and min of 0, and a Reading of 114.  These are populated just before the code you've changed here
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/82a92ac8e45e82cb654a89bc987c767a614ea909/redfish-core/include/utils/sensor_utils.hpp#L918

Hummm. I am not sure here. I did not added these "ReadingRangeMin/Max" and "ReadingRangeMax" attributes. Looking at https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Sensor/Value.interface.yaml such attributes are not even supported by the value interface. I am suspecting bmcweb is just defaulting to 0.

But again, I would consider that unrelated to this change right?

> Hummm. I am not sure here. I did not added these "ReadingRangeMin/Max" and "ReadingRangeMax" attributes. Looking at https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Sensor/Value.interface.yaml
> such attributes are not even supported by the value interface. I am suspecting bmcweb is just defaulting to 0.

yes, they are, they're sourced from MinValue and MaxValue.

I'm not aware of any code that defaults these values to 0.0, and any code would be in the block you modified here.

> 
> But again, I would consider that unrelated to this change right?

You're changing the behavior of how these properties operate, so no, I would assume it's related until we know otherwise.

The min/max are unrelated to Amithash's change and are an artifact of our system.  I check one without his change and it has the same.  Digging into it, these are sensors created by PLDM and the min/max values are likely not being filled in by the PLDM device in this case.  The Sensor.Value from PLDM has 0.0 for both min and max.

For the sensor subsystem, "not filled in" value is a NaN, not 0.  If we're seeing a 0 in the Redfish response (either before or after his change) it isn't a not filled in, but either a "filled in and zero" or a "filled in incorrectly".
Acknowledged

> I check one without his change and it has the same

That's good enough for me.

Sounds like a bug in PLDM we need to fix.

Looking at this, is this valid for ALL the sensor properties?

For MaxValue and MinValue, they default to -infinity and +infinity.  For those default cases, I would assume we would want to completely omit the properties rather than include them and have them be null?

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Sensor/Value.interface.yaml#L32

Thats true for the thresholds as well
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/tree/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Sensor/Threshold/*.yaml
which default to NaN.

Are you suggesting instead to just delete the 
```
BMCWEB_LOG_WARNING("Sensor value for {} was unexpectedly {}",
                                   valueName, *doubleValue);
```
line and call it good?

No, I'm suggesting we need to go through each property and determine what the behavior is.  The commit message talks about changing thresholds, which is fine, but functionally this patch is changing behavior for every property across 4 resource classes.  I'd like at least some analysis that we're doing the right thing here.

In general the "not populated" defaults shouldn't show up on Redfish, so at a minimum you'd need to keep MinValue/MaxValue in this check.

Thresholds are different in that a user might want to modify them, so I'm happy to see them have different rules, but the point is we need to consider all the properties that flow through this.
ok. so something more like https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/86007/3 but one set which allows nan and another set which skips.

Yeah, that patch was closer to what I'd expect.  MOST importantly is that you've done some rudimentary analysis of all the properties that flow through this code and we have some understanding that what you did was correct for all of them.  Ideally we'd have unit tests for this stuff, but here we are.

We'll never be perfect, and this isn't intended to be exhaustive, but the commit message makes it sound like only thresholds on sensor were considered, whereas the patchset changes all the properties.

FWIW, I had forgotten the history here.  I suspect the code we have now is fine, just need a commit message that talks about what properties we're functionally changing, and what the new behavior will be.

Done! I updated the change to split the groups of properties into two categories of "ok if undefined by service".
One which if undefined by the service, we should allow it to be present with a 'null' value. And a second where if its undefined, its compleltey absent from the proprities list.

Also updated the commit message to represent this change in the start so thats first before the reasoning and the tests.

FWIW, this code has now defeated the purpose of hanving a common path for all the floating point values, and could be cleaned up in the future to just do what the other handlers do, loop over each key, and do the transforms in helper functions as needed.

Oh well, we're here now, and I don't want to hold this up any longer than I already have.
